scope: Independent raw-log/resource/hash audit; no model/native regrade

clauses.basis: Issue: after `$ans.last | str length` fails with only_supports_this_input_type, `$ans` is broken. maybe_store_last_result only skips bare $ans expressions, so the failing pipeline's output (error values) replaces `.last`. On baseline `$ans.last` becomes a list of Error values (observed). Expected: `$ans` and its `.last` remain the prior valid result, both for value and streamed sources.
A valid transform of `$ans.last` (e.g. `| first`) must still update the stored last result; existing test transform_of_last_updates_store covers the same behavior.
Whether `$ans.last` should ever hold a partially-successful stream with some error items, or how errors should be surfaced/stored, is not specified by the issue.

Issue: with max_last_result_size > 0, a failing `$ans.last | str length` (only_supports_this_input_type on record rows) makes a later `$ans` raise the same error; expected behavior is that fetching `$ans` is not broken. Baseline trace: `str length` returns a per-item Value::error rather than Err, so the stream only fails when printed; `maybe_store_last_result` -> `store_list_stream_prefix` has already stored those error items into `$ans.last` (maybe_store_last_result is documented as storing 'the successful interactive pipeline result'). Rendering `$ans` with the default display_output branch `table -e` (wide terminal) then expands `last` and raises the stored error. Observed on baseline: `$ans | table -e` evaluated via eval_block returns Err(OnlySupportsThisInputType { exp_input_type: "string", wrong_type: "record<a: int>" }) after the failing line. The test asserts only that `$ans` renders without error; it does not assert what `$ans.last` holds. eval_source's exit code is not usable here because it returns 0 even when rendering `$ans` printed the error.

The same defect observed at the stored value: on baseline, after `[{a: 1} {a: 2}]` then `$ans.last | str length`, `$ans.last` is List([Error(OnlySupportsThisInputType), Error(OnlySupportsThisInputType)]). A failed line is not a 'successful interactive pipeline result' (doc of maybe_store_last_result) and the existing test error_does_not_overwrite shows failed lines are not meant to put a failure into `$ans`. The test asserts only that `$ans` contains no Value::Error anywhere after the failed line; it is agnostic to whether the previous `.last`, an empty/partial value, or no `last` is kept.

Invalid operations on `$ans.last` must keep failing, and failures that already behave correctly must stay so. Observed on baseline: `$ans.last | first | str length` (single-value failure) exits nonzero, leaves `$ans.last` equal to the earlier list, and `$ans` still renders under `table -e`; the streamed `$ans.last | str length` line itself still exits nonzero. A repair that swallows the error or clears `.last` on every failure would regress this (compare existing test error_does_not_overwrite for top-level errors).

Successful transforms of `$ans.last` that flow through a list stream must still be stored and `$ans` must still render. Observed on baseline: after `["a" "bcd"]`, `$ans.last | str length` exits 0, `$ans.last` becomes [1 3] and `$ans | table -e` renders. Guards against a repair that stops storing stream results or drops them whenever any error check is added. Related existing behavior: transform_of_last_updates_store and truncated_list_prefix_respects_byte_budget.

What `$ans.last` should hold after the failed stream line is not stated by the issue. Plausible, incompatible outcomes: the previous result kept (as a failed top-level line does today and as the single-value failure does), an empty or partial prefix of the stream, or no `last` field at all (so a later `$ans.last` would be a missing-column error). Public evidence only requires `$ans` not to be broken, so no assertion is made.

The issue says the reporter can so far reproduce only with only_supports_this_input_type. A baseline probe (not kept as a test) showed the same stored-error mechanism for other failing streams, e.g. `$ans.last | each {|x| error make {msg: boom}}` and `[{a: 1}] | str length` as a first line, but expected behavior for those, and for streams with both valid and failing items, is not stated, so no assertion is made.

scientific_decision: NO-GO for baseline-only oracle authoring on this development case; not a general low-vs-xhigh capability claim
